sections.label: Lee Li Lian oath NCMP seat
sections.summary: Ms Lee Li Lian did not take the oath of allegiance at the First Session's first or second Sittings and decided not to take up her NCMP seat.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: With reference to section 53 of the said Act, I also wish to state for the record that Ms Lee Li Lian did not take and subscribe the oath of allegiance before this Parliament at its first or second Sittings in its First Session held on 15 January 2016 and 25 January 2016, respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ms Lee Li Lian of the Workers' Party was declared an NCMP at the General Elections 2015 but has decided not to take up the seat.

sections.label: Filling vacant East Coast NCMP seat
sections.summary: Only one candidate instead of two was declared NCMP for East Coast GRC, so Parliament should consider declaring another candidate from that team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a result, East Coast GRC despite being qualified as the next succeeding GRC, only one candidate instead of two was declared NCMP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the circumstances, it is logical that Parliament consider filling the vacant seat by declaring another candidate from the East Coast GRC team as NCMP.

sections.label: Prime Minister on NCMP scheme
sections.summary: The Prime Minister explained the NCMP scheme's purpose and indicated intention to increase Opposition Members and give NCMPs equal voting rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister, on Wednesday, had given a detailed explanation of the purpose of the NCMP scheme and indicated his intention to increase the number of Opposition Members in this House and to give NCMPs voting rights equal to constituency Members of Parliament.

sections.label: Respecting minority vote and NCMP transfer
sections.summary: The passage says the minority's decision and Punggol East SMC voting results must be respected, and the Act does not let parties pick best losers from different constituencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Insofar as the NCMP scheme is concerned, while we must indeed respect the decision of the majority in our General Elections, which was the first of the reasons Ms Lee gave for declining the seat, we must also accord sufficient respect to the decision of the minority as provided for in our statutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: This means, in this case, respecting the results of voting in Punggol East SMC, which saw sufficient numbers of voters in my constituency giving Ms Lee Li Lian a mandate to enter Parliament, a privilege which she has, regretfully, declined to accept and one which the Workers' Party now seeks to transfer to another candidate who did not qualify on the basis of the GE results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: As pointed out by Mr Low Thia Khiang, while the Parliamentary Elections Act allow for Opposition parties to nominate the NCMPs where a GRC is concerned, the Act is really not intended to allow Opposition parties to pick and choose which best losers from different constituencies to enter Parliament.

sections.label: Reviewing vacated NCMP seat provisions
sections.summary: The passage urges the Workers' Party to play by the NCMP rules and suggests reviewing provisions for filling a vacated NCMP seat to prevent abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: It is clear that there is a precedence within the Workers' Party for declining an NCMP position and still retaining your party membership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: But whatever their internal positions and intentions may be, as the members of the Workers' Party have now largely seem to accept the NCMP scheme, I would urge them to play by its rules, to abide by its spirit and not to use non-acceptance of a seat by properly-elected candidates as a backdoor way to have someone who did not qualify for the position into this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister has now announced that the NCMP scheme will be tweaked, it seems to me an opportune time for the Government to review the provisions relating to filling a vacated NCMP seat to prevent abuse of the current system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: In particular, the practice of transferring an NCMP seat to a candidate in a different constituency is not sound in principle.

sections.label: Clarifying Workers' Party NCMP transfer position
sections.summary: The passage asks the Workers' Party to clarify its position on transferring NCMP seats so Members can make a more informed decision on the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: In the light of these concerns, I would like the Workers' Party to clarify their position on the transfer of NCMP seats, so that Members, in consideration of the Motion, can make a more informed decision of the factors prompting the request of the filling of the vacated seat with another Workers' Party candidate.

sections.label: Reservations on supporting Motion
sections.summary: The speaker says voting against the Motion would harm debate and diversity, but has difficulty supporting it without reservations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: While voting against the Motion would not be in the interest of debate and diversity of voices in this House, this is a Motion that I have difficulty supporting as it stands without expressing my reservations.

sections.label: WP members accepting NCMP seats
sections.summary: Since 2006, five WP members have accepted the NCMP seat.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Since 2006, there have been five WP members who had accepted the NCMP seat.

sections.label: WP recommends Daniel Goh as NCMP
sections.summary: WP has recommended Mr Daniel Goh to take over Ms Lee Li Lian as an NCMP.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: WP has recommended Mr Daniel Goh to take over Ms Lee Li Lian as an NCMP.

sections.label: Eight Opposition Members already in Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker says with eight Opposition Members now, allowing an NCMP seat to be filled may not be needed.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If there are only three Opposition Members in Parliament now, then perhaps for the sake of having enough Opposition Members, we can allow one of the NCMP seats to be filled.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But now, we already have a total of eight Opposition Members.

sections.label: Review legislation for NCMP legitimacy
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will review relevant legislation to ensure the NCMP seat maintains its legitimacy.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, the legitimacy and the appointment of the NCMP will become more important.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can review the relevant legislation to make sure that the NCMP seat will maintain its legitimacy.

sections.label: WP stance on NCMP scheme
sections.summary: The speaker hopes WP will clarify whether its candidates will fulfil their duties under the NCMP system next election.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister mentioned two days ago that the Government would confer NCMPs the same voting rights as elected Members and will increase the minimum number of Opposition Members in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means that the NCMP scheme will become even more important.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, I hope that the WP will be able to clarify their stance regarding the NCMP scheme.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the next election, will they ensure that all their candidates are prepared to fulfil their duties towards the voters under the system?

sections.label: NCMP seat declared vacant
sections.summary: The Workers' Party said Daniel Goh would fill the seat after MPD Nair did not take the oath, and no by-election was held.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Party had earlier announced that should Parliament declare the vacancy and resolve that it be filled, Assoc Prof Daniel Goh would fill the seat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At that election, the Workers' Party candidate, Mr MPD Nair was offered an NCMP seat, having narrowly lost the contest in Jalan Kayu by 571 votes, out of about 23, 400.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When Mr MPD Nair did not subscribe to the oath of allegiance in the first two Sittings of Parliament, then Leader of the House, Mr S Dhanabalan moved the Motion to declare the seat vacant and to have it filled by the next succeeding candidate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: No by-election was held in that instance to fill the seat.

sections.label: Dhanabalan moves filling Motion
sections.summary: Minister S Dhanabalan moved the Motion to provide for filling the vacant NCMP seat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: Back then, the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Minister for Community Development Mr S Dhanabalan moved the Motion stating that it is to provide for the filling of the vacant NCMP seat.

sections.label: PAP amended law 2010
sections.summary: The PAP Government amended the law in 2010 to allow up to nine Opposition Members, and the Workers' Party says the NCMP scheme is unnecessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: The PAP Government of today believes it could retain its influence and power with up to nine Opposition Members in Parliament and amended the law in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: This Motion does not change in any way the stand of the Workers' Party that the NCMP scheme is not necessary if we had adhered to our original Constitution and reverted to a democracy comprising only Single Member Constituencies.

sections.label: Workers' Party implements section 53
sections.summary: The Workers' Party says it respects its members' wishes and is implementing section 53 of the Parliamentary Elections Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: The Workers' Party respects the wishes of its members and I am sure the PAP will do the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: So, this is what the Workers' Party is doing today and that is to implement to the letter of the law what is provided in section 53 of the Parliamentary Elections Act.

sections.label: PM proposes more NCMPs
sections.summary: The Prime Minister proposed increasing NCMPs from nine to 12 and giving them equal voting rights, which could mean 20% non-governing-party Members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Two days ago, the Prime Minister proposed to further strengthen this scheme by further increasing the number NCMPs from nine to 12, and also to give NCMPs equal voting rights as those of elected MPs in this House.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If Parliament accepts our Prime Minister's proposal, it will mean that 20% of this House will come from parties other than the governing party, in any electoral circumstances, even in extreme circumstances where one party wins all 89 seats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Second, there will be no difference between elected MPs and elected, I say "elected", NCMPs.

sections.label: Sylvia Lim on NCMPs
sections.summary: In 2010, Ms Sylvia Lim said having more NCMPs is not the way forward to make the political system more robust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In 2010, Ms Sylvia Lim said that having more NCMPs is not the way forward to make our political system more robust.

sections.label: Jeyaretnam and NCMP scheme
sections.summary: Mr JB Jeyaretnam, who said in 1984 he wanted nothing to do with the NCMP scheme, accepted the seat himself in 1997 when offered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Mr JB Jeyaretnam who claimed that he wanted nothing to do with the NCMP scheme in 1984 accepted the seat himself in 1997 when it was offered to him.

sections.label: Lee calls scheme supportable
sections.summary: In 2009 she said the scheme is overall supportable because it gives greater recognition to voters for Opposition candidates who would be shut out.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In 2009, she said the scheme is "overall supportable" because it gives "greater recognition to the desire of voters who cast votes for Opposition candidates in significant numbers which would otherwise be shut out in a pure first-past-the-post system".

sections.label: Lee rejecting NCMP seat
sections.summary: The question is why Ms Lee, the Workers' Party candidate closest to re-election, decided not to fulfil her responsibility to Punggol East voters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: So, the question is: why did Ms Lee, a Member of this House in the last Parliament, the Workers' Party candidate who came closest to being re-elected and returned to Parliament, decide not to fulfil her responsibility to the people of Punggol East who had voted for her?

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It is most regrettable that Ms Lee has chosen to reject her NCMP seat and, with that, her responsibility to her voters and Singapore.

sections.label: Low dismissing NCMP scheme
sections.summary: On the same night the Prime Minister explained expanding the NCMP scheme, Mr Low completely dismissed it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: When the Prime Minister on Wednesday gave his speech and explained why we are going to expand the NCMP scheme in size and in scope, on the very same night, Mr Low completely dismissed the NCMP scheme.

sections.label: Supporting filling last NCMP seat
sections.summary: The party will support filling the last NCMP seat according to the rules, noting the Workers' Party criticised the system yet used it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Why do we want Mr Leon Perera, Mr Dennis Tan and, perhaps, in time to come, Mr Daniel Goh, to spend their precious time to be here, if it is of no political advantage for the Workers' Party?

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: So, Madam, for this reason, my party will support the filling of the last NCMP seat according to the rules.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have to recognise that the Workers' Party has continued to criticise the system and, yet, deliberately made use of it to the hilt for its political advantage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As such, Mdm Speaker, with your permission I propose to amend the Motion with the following additions.

sections.label: Amendment on Lee giving up seat
sections.summary: An amendment regrets Ms Lee giving up her NCMP seat to a party candidate with a lower vote share, contrary to voters' will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: With that, Madam, I beg to move the Motion as amended.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: It has been proposed, as an amendment, that the words "(c) but regrets that Ms Lee Li Lian, having stood as a Workers' Party candidate and received the highest vote share among all losing Opposition candidates has now decided to give up her NCMP seat to another candidate from her party with a lower vote share, contrary to the expressed will of the voters, and that the Workers' Party supports this political manoeuvre to take full advantage of the NCMP seat, even as its Secretary General criticises NCMPs as just 'duckweed on the water of the pond.'", and these words be added at the end of the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Hon Members, it may be convenient that the debate on the original Motion and on any other amendments moved by Members be proceeded with simultaneously as a debate on a single Question.

sections.label: PAP benefit from NCMP scheme
sections.summary: The speaker says the PAP does not benefit from the NCMP scheme, but he sees a benefit to the PAP not to Singapore's benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is been put across that the People's Action Party does not stand to benefit in any way from the NCMP scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But, Mdm Speaker, I do see a benefit to the People's Action Party that is not to the benefit of Singapore.

sections.label: PAP hyper majority in Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker says if politics evolves with no elected Opposition MPs, the PAP would have a hyper majority, which he says is not a super majority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If Singapore's politics evolves, so that there are no elected Opposition MPs – which could well be a reality, it nearly happened in the last general election – what will happen is that the People's Action Party's hyper majority in Parliament – it is not a super majority; "super majority" is a term that comes from US politics and I think it refers to a 60% majority in the Senate, this is not a "super majority", Mdm Speaker.

sections.label: Opposition to NCMP scheme
sections.summary: The speaker fears there will be no viable constructive Opposition to hold the Government to account, so he opposes the NCMP scheme in principle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: There will not be an electable and viable constructive Opposition party that Singaporeans will be able to support in order to hold the Government to account and ensure that the Government actually aligns itself to the political character of the country and the will of the people of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: That is my fear for Singapore and that is why I oppose the NCMP scheme in principle.

sections.label: Dependence on one party
sections.summary: The speaker asks what happens if Singapore depends on one party overwhelmingly and that party fails with no other party to step in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: But is the thrust of this Motion for the good of Singapore, or is it really undermining the long-term democratic hopes that I certainly would have for real democracy and for balance in this country?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: And this one question is this and it has not been answered to the best of my knowledge by the hon Members of the People's Action Party who have spoken, which is, what will happen to Singapore if we are dependent on just one party overwhelmingly and that one party fails and there is no other party in our political landscape that can step in to remedy that gap?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: If you feel that that is an argument to develop more political balance, as I do, then that should be the consideration that guides us to have a political landscape that encourages the development of real political balance.

sections.label: Lee Li Lian declining NCMP seat
sections.summary: The speaker says Ms Lee Li Lian did not accept the NCMP seat, and it was not because the party asked her to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: First of all, Ms Lee Li Lian did not accept the NCMP seat not because the party asked her to do so.

sections.label: Lee Li Lian and Punggol East voters
sections.summary: The speaker says Ms Lee decided that Punggol East voters' rejection meant she had no legitimacy to be in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: Members are saying here that, "Look, you don't take Punggol East voters seriously, you don't respect them".

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: It is exactly because Ms Lee did not and would not take lightly the voters of Punggol East, that she decided having been their elected MP for over two years, their rejection means she has no legitimacy to be in Parliament.

sections.label: NCMP compared to duckweed
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker compared an NCMP to duckweed and that NCMPs cannot do many things elected MPs can.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: The last part of the amended Motion, referring to what I said to the press, that I compared an NCMP to "duckweed on the water of the pond".

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: There is a fundamental difference between an NCMP and an elected MP, or a constituency MP because there are a lot of things you cannot do as an NCMP.

sections.label: Opposition MPs real power
sections.summary: A functional democracy's Parliament must give Opposition MPs real power to check and contest with the Ruling party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: A Parliament of a functional democracy must give Opposition MPs real power to check and to contest with the Ruling party of the day to hold the Government accountable.

sections.label: Amended Motion put to vote
sections.summary: The amendment was agreed to, a consequential amendment will be made, and the amended Motion will be voted on.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: As the amendment has been agreed to, the necessary consequential amendment to the Motion will be made.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: I will now put the Motion, as amended, for Members' vote.

sections.label: Abstaining on paragraph (c)
sections.summary: Objection to paragraph (c) was recorded, so they will abstain and a show of hands will record abstentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: Since our objection on paragraph (c) has been recorded, we will abstain from voting, instead of objecting.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Can I have a show of hands as to who is abstaining, for us to record?

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: I will take note of the abstentions on this side of the House       [(proc text) (a) declares that the seat of Ms Lee Li Lian, who was elected a non-constituency Member of Parliament under section 52 of the Act, has become vacant by reason of her having failed to take and subscribe before Parliament the Oath of Allegiance under Article 61 of the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore at the first and second Sittings of the first session of the present Parliament; and (proc text)]   [(proc text) (c) but regrets that Ms Lee Li Lian, having stood as a Workers' Party candidate and received the highest vote share among all losing Opposition candidates, has now decided to give up her NCMP seat to another candidate from her party with a lower vote share, contrary to the expressed will of the voters, and that the Workers' Party supports this political manoeuvre to take full advantage of the NCMP seat, even as its Secretary General criticises NCMPs as just 'duckweed on the water of the pond.' " (proc text)]
